record.original_question: For the Engel distribution, that is, a rank-2 distribution in ℝ4 with n3(q) = 3 and n4(q) = 4, what is the C1 classification of the germs of sub-Riemannian spheres at points lying on the optimal singular curve through the point? Equivalently, how should one classify these 3-dimensional hypersurface singularities in ℝ4 up to local C1 diffeomorphism?

evidence.quote: The next step is the Engel distribution, i. e. a rank 2 distribution in R4 such that n3(q) = 3, n4(q) = 4. There is exactly one singular curve through any point and small segments of singular curves are optimal. We repeat our question for this case; the spheres are now 3-dimensional hypersurfaces in R4.
Hence the solution of the problem in the 4-dimensional Engel case is a very important step in the unfolding of the sphere for any n ≥ 4.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Delta$ be a rank-2 distribution on $\mathbb{R}^4$ (a smooth subbundle of rank 2 of $T\mathbb{R}^4$) endowed with a smooth sub-Riemannian metric $g$ on $\Delta$. For a point $q\in\mathbb{R}^4$, let $\Delta^1(q)=\Delta(q)$ and inductively define $\Delta^{k+1}(q)=\Delta^k(q)+[\Delta,\Delta^k](q)$, and set $n_k(q)=\dim\Delta^k(q)$. Assume that at every point $q\in\mathbb{R}^4$ one has $n_2(q)=3$ and $n_3(q)=4$ (the Engel condition; equivalently, $\Delta$ is an Engel distribution).

For such a structure, through every point $q_0$ there passes a unique (up to reparametrization) singular (abnormal) horizontal curve, and sufficiently small arcs of this curve are length-minimizing. For $r>0$ small, let $S_r(q_0)\subset\mathbb{R}^4$ denote the sub-Riemannian sphere of radius $r$ centered at $q_0$, i.e. the set of points whose sub-Riemannian distance from $q_0$ equals $r$. Let $q\in S_r(q_0)$ be a point lying on the singular curve through $q_0$.

Problem. Classify, up to local $C^1$-diffeomorphism of $(\mathbb{R}^4, q)$, the germs at $q$ of the 3-dimensional hypersurface singularities $S_r(q_0)$ that arise in this Engel setting.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g. Ardentov–Sachkov on the flat Engel sub-Riemannian sphere, and studies on front asymptotics near abnormal geodesics) describes the asymptotics and shows non-subanalyticity of the Engel sphere at the abnormal poles, but no full local $C^1$ classification of these hypersurface singularities appears to be available. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Front Asymptotics of a Flat Sub-Riemannian Structure on the Engel Distribution
status_evidence.snippet: The front of a flat sub-Riemannian structure on the Engel distribution in a neighborhood of a non-subanalytic singularity is approximated... the sphere is not subanalytic at the poles.
status_evidence.claim: Engel sphere singularities at abnormal poles are studied asymptotically and shown to be non-subanalytic, but only asymptotic models are obtained, not a $C^1$ classification.

status_evidence.title: Sub-Riemannian Engel Sphere (ResearchGate)
status_evidence.snippet: The sub-Riemannian distance has very complicated and mysterious singularities along abnormal geodesics in the Engel case.
status_evidence.claim: The structure of singularities of the Engel sub-Riemannian sphere along abnormal curves is described as complicated and not yet classified.
